chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Chicago musicians play for the soloist
summary: DeMichael and Saunders agree Chicago rhythm sections are accommodating to visiting stars like Dexter Gordon and Teddy Wilson.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: There's something else I've noticed about Chicago musicians, and I wondered if you agree with it, is that Chicago musicians, as you say, are competitive, but they're also accommodating, in the sense that -- say Dexter Gordon comes in.
And so there's Wilbur Campbell and maybe John Young.
Dan Shapiro in the rhythm section.
And the guys will play for the soloist rather than play for themselves.
But you see that in other instances, in shows, for instance, when you play for shows. You see it in the symphony orchestra, of being able to interpret and play what's expected.

Right, there's a certain amount of pride in the musicians here. They -- the product, regardless of who's fronting it, the product has got to be good. This is the attitude that they -- and the thing that I think they strive for.
That's very good, because it's just like you say, they play for the individual, don't care who it is, and so they don't go into this bag of starring themselves.
They can change what they might have done --
Before, right, and to fit within what he's doing.

So this is why you find all of these guys who come in here and they augment with them, like Teddy Wilson and -- well, Dorothy or whoever it is, if he comes in town, and they augment with them, from local musicians. They're very, very satisfied. Marian McPartland, all of those, they're very, very, very satisfied with what they--
